Definition: from a derivative of a compound of G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G1311; incorruptibleness, i.e. (figuratively) purity (of doctrine):--uncorruptness.
BiblicalUsage: Adiaphthoria appears once, in Paul's instruction to Titus: show yourself a pattern of good works, 'in doctrine shewing uncorruptness, gravity, sincerity.' The word means incorruptness — teaching that has not been spoiled or watered down. A young leader's doctrine is to be sound all the way through, with nothing rotten in it.
TheologicalSignificance: I won't squeeze theology out of a word that was written to name a thing plainly — the verse around it does the teaching; in this case, the verse is Titus 2:7.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
